meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Эффектная подача блюд делает их вкуснее.
examples.trans: Spectacular presentation of dishes makes them tastier.
You know what, give me a coffee.

examples.text: Кофе? Да, дайте мне кофе эспрессо.
examples.trans: Coffee? Yes, give me an espresso coffee.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important, mattering').

examples.text: Что самое важное в работе официанта?
examples.trans: What is the most important thing in a waiter's job?
One very important ingredient is missing.

examples.text: Извините. Только назову тебе очень важный ингредиент.
examples.trans: Excuse me. Only I will name the very important ingredient for you.

meanings.en: to go, to set off (by car, bus, train)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'let's go, drove off', paired with 'ехать'.

examples.trans: Well then, shall we go?
It doesn't matter. Let's go home.
We'll go home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'home', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It doesn't matter. Let's go home.

examples.text: Раз вы меня ограбить начали, давайте я вас обедом угощу.
examples.trans: Since you have started to rob me, let me treat you to lunch.

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attention' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Attention, the results!
May I have your attention.
Thank you for your attention.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'results' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я жду только одного — результатов от вас.
examples.trans: I expect only one thing: results from you.

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'step out, come out', paired with 'выйти'.

examples.trans: Step out. Quiet!
I'm going out in a minute.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
